 “An Attitude of Gratitude” on Morning Energy
 Posted on November 20, 2026 • by Renna Reddick 
 Share 
 “Gratitude turns what we have into enough.” — Melody Beattie 
 Thanksgiving is a nationwide celebration and federal holiday in the United States, observed annually on the fourth Thursday of November. The Thanksgiving season is often associated with heavy travel, family traditions, community giving, and expressions of deep gratitude.
 According to research conducted by the Pew Research Center, 78% of U.S. adults reported experiencing a deep sense of gratitude at least once a week. There are countless reasons people may experience gratitude, whether it’s spending time with loved ones, receiving an unexpected act of kindness from a stranger, or simply making it through a difficult day.
 But here’s something worth considering: Are these occasional experiences of gratitude enough, or can we develop a deeper, more enduring sense of appreciation that becomes part of our everyday lives?
 On this week’s Morning Energy , we’re going to explore how we can move beyond those occasional feelings of gratitude that often accompany the holiday season or arise when something wonderful happens. Instead, we’ll examine how we can cultivate a lasting tendency to recognize, appreciate, and express gratitude for the good that already exists in our lives.
 Join me this Friday from 4–6 a.m. for a very special musical journey as we explore this inspiring and thought-provoking topic.
 And if you miss the live program, you can always listen to the weekly broadcast for up to seven days through the archives at WMNF (https://www.wmnf.org/events/morning-energy/).
